title: Adaptive locale-conditioned hybrid reranker selector and staged upgrade plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Introduce an adaptive selector for cross-encoder rerankers that chooses between compact / quantized variants and full-precision models per-request based on locale, latency budget, and quality risk. The selector should enable staged upgrades with per-locale canaries and automatic fallback to stable variants when regression signals are detected. Background: We currently run a single cross-encoder family for rerank endpoints with occasional manual rollouts. International locales show varying quality sensitivity and latency profiles; some locales tolerate compact models without MRR loss while others degrade. This ticket defines selection rules, regression checks, rollout plan, and instrumentation required to safely upgrade to new cross-encoder variants (including q4_0/q8_0 quantized families and smaller multilingual cross-encoders).

Proposal summary:
- Implement a lightweight request-level selector service (in-ring microservice) that returns a reranker variant key given metadata: locale, route, latency_slo_ms, token_budget, and past-model-score-deltas. Selector logic will be rule-based initially with thresholds and a simple probabilistic weight for exploring new variants.
- Define per-locale quality tiers (conservative / balanced / exploratory). Default conservative for locales with <10k monthly queries or high variance in evals.
- Create a regression harness that runs 100k simulated requests per variant per locale using our offline eval prompt set and holds-out a set of reference queries. Metrics: MRR@10, nDCG, average latency p50/p95, cost-per-query, and token-efficiency delta vs baseline.
- Acceptance gates: no more than 0.5% absolute MRR drop in conservative locales, no more than 1.0% in balanced, and regression alerts for exploratory locales with >1.5% drop.
- Rollout strategy: staged canary by traffic slice and locale (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback if regression detectors trigger during any step.
- Observability: extend Console to show per-variant, per-locale MRR deltas, latency percentiles, and a variant fallback counter. Add tracing tags to link selector decisions to backend model variant used.
- KV warmstart and caching: evaluate impact of KV caching on latency for quantized models; add warmstart prefetch for canary traffic to avoid cold-start skew.

Implementation tasks (high level):
1) Selector service prototype (Marco) - rule engine + sampling, config API for per-locale tiers
2) Offline regression harness (SRE + Marco) - dataset orchestration, batch runs, baseline comparison scripts
3) Instrumentation (Observability team) - dashboard panels, traces, cost breakdown per-variant
4) Rollout automation (Platform) - create canary controller with automated stop/rollback hooks tied to regression alerts
5) Eval and smoke tests (QA) - smoke suite for top 30 locales and latency budget tests under concurrency
6) Docs & runbook (PM + Eng) - rollout checklist, rollback actions, stakeholder notifications

Success criteria:
- Demonstrated ability to safely shift 50% of global rerank traffic to compact/quantized variants without exceeding defined MRR degradation targets
- Dashboard showing per-locale MRR deltas and automated alerts firing (and not firing) during rollouts
- Rollout controller used for one complete upgrade with automated rollback exercised in staging

Risks & mitigations:
- Spurious regressions due to dataset drift: mitigate by expanding reference sets and adding temporal weighting to regression metrics
- Latency variability from quantization on specific GPU types: run hardware-specific microbenchmarks and add hardware-aware rules in selector
- Increased complexity of debugging root cause: ensure tracing and variant tags are present end-to-end and capture candidate features used for selection

Notes about scope and non-goals:
- We are not building a full ML bandit optimizer in this ticket; sampling is simple epsilon-based exploration for safety. Full optimization and continuous learning will be planned in follow-up work.
- This ticket focuses on cross-encoder rerankers and multilingual variants; we will not change embedding models in this rollout.

Links & artifacts:
- Offline eval dataset: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/rerank/offline-evals/locale_reference_v2.csv
- Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RERANK/Locale+Adaptive+Reranker+Playbook
- Prototype selector PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/896
- Dashboard mockups: https://figma.com/redwood/rerank-rollout-dashboards

If accepted, next action: schedule a 60-minute sync with Observability and Platform to agree alert conditions and canary controller API (owner: Marco).
comments: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial scoping and acceptance gates drafted. Recommended per-locale tiers based on query volume and variance.

2026-03-04 SRE (review): Ran microbenchmarks for q8_0 on gpus-rtx-a5000; p50 latency +6ms vs baseline, p95 +18ms under small batches. Noted KV warmstart mitigates p95 for steady traffic. Added to dependency notes.

2026-03-09 Observability: Dashboard scaffolding merged, variant-level metrics emitted. Endpoint: /dashboards/rerank/variant-breakdown. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1123.

2026-03-11 Marco Liu: Added fallback counter and forced-fallback mode for canary tests. Prepared canary slices (5%,20%,50%). Plan to run canary in staging next week and execute automated rollback if MRR breach persists beyond 10,000 queries.

2026-03-12 PM (Lena Gomez): Approved rollout plan pending SRE signoff on hardware microbenchmarks and a run of the regression harness across top-30 locales. Scheduled sync with Observability and Platform 2026-03-15.
